parameters.content:
## Invoice Processing Automation Workflow

Starter template from agentmelt.com — configure before running:

1. Fill in "Config (edit me)" (name, approver, quiet hours; test_mode stays on for the first week).
2. Add credentials to every service node (Anthropic, mail, CRM, database…).
3. Replace placeholder URLs, queries and field mappings with yours.
4. Set the trigger: New attachments to ap@ start the run; supplier portals and scanned batches are polled hourly.
5. Keep the gates: 'Needs a person?' after every AI step, 'Approved?' after the approval — wire their dead ends to a sheet or a channel.
6. Keep the guardrails:
   - Bank-detail changes never post automatically; they trigger a verification call with the supplier.
   - Auto-approval applies only to PO-matched invoices within tolerance and policy limits; everything else has a named approver.
   - Duplicates are blocked before posting, not caught at month end.
   - Low-confidence extractions are reviewed by a person before matching.

Full blueprint and pricing: https://agentmelt.com/workflows/invoice-processing-automation/
Want it built and run for you? $297/month · custom $5,000–9,000 one-time

nodes.name: Gmail Trigger: Capture the invoice
nodes.notes:
Capture the invoice

PDF, image or e-invoice attachment saved to a document store with the email metadata; non-invoice attachments are classified and filed elsewhere.

assignments.name: config.your_name
assignments.value: Your name — signs every outgoing message

assignments.name: config.approver
assignments.value: #approvals — a Slack channel, or an email address

nodes.name: Config (edit me)
nodes.notes:
Fill these in once; every later node reads them as $('Config (edit me)').item.json.config.*

test_mode = true: log what the workflow would write, without writing it, for the first week.
approval_mode = true: the approval node waits for a person; switch off per message type once it has earned it.

Also point the nodes at your own sources:
- AP inbox and supplier portals
- ERP: POs, receipts, supplier master, GL, approval policy
- Historic coding for non-PO invoices
- Bank-detail master for fraud checks

options.systemPromptTemplate: Supplier, invoice number, dates, line items, quantities, unit prices, tax, totals, PO reference and bank details, with a confidence per field. Multi-page and multi-currency handled.

nodes.name: Information Extractor: Extract fields
nodes.notes:
Extract fields

Supplier, invoice number, dates, line items, quantities, unit prices, tax, totals, PO reference and bank details, with a confidence per field. Multi-page and multi-currency handled.

nodes.name: Needs a person?
nodes.notes: True = the AI step was not sure or flagged the item → dead letter, a person looks. False = continue. Wire the dead letter to a Slack message or a sheet so nothing fails silently.

nodes.name: Needs a person: Extract fields
nodes.notes: Dead letter. Replace this no-op with a Slack message or a sheet row that carries the raw item and the reason — silent failures are the ones that cost.

nodes.name: Code: Validate and detect duplicates
nodes.notes:
Validate and detect duplicates

Totals foot, tax is arithmetically right, supplier exists (or is flagged as new), bank details match the master (change = fraud alert), and no invoice with the same supplier + number + amount exists.

parameters.notes: Three-way match against the ERP: PO lines, quantities received, prices within tolerance. Non-PO invoices are coded by the agent from supplier history and GL rules.

nodes.name: HTTP Request: Match to PO and receipt
nodes.notes:
Match to PO and receipt

Three-way match against the ERP: PO lines, quantities received, prices within tolerance. Non-PO invoices are coded by the agent from supplier history and GL rules.

nodes.name: Switch: Route exceptions and approvals
nodes.notes:
Route exceptions and approvals

Clean matches auto-approve within policy limits; mismatches go to the buyer with the specific difference; non-PO invoices go to the cost-centre owner; new suppliers go to procurement for onboarding.

nodes.name: Slack approval: Approve on the phone
nodes.notes:
Approve on the phone

Approvers get the invoice summary and the exception in Slack or email with approve/reject/query buttons; reminders escalate after the SLA.

Send-and-wait: the run pauses here until someone presses Approve or Reject. Set config.approver in "Config (edit me)".

nodes.name: Approved?
nodes.notes: True = approved → continue to the write-back. False = rejected → stop here; the item stays where it was.

nodes.name: Rejected: Approve on the phone
nodes.notes: Rejected by the approver. Nothing is written. Optionally log the rejection to your sheet so the weekly count of corrections is visible.

parameters.notes: Approved invoices are created in NetSuite, Xero, QuickBooks, Sage or SAP with coding, attachments and the approval trail; payment runs pick them up.

nodes.name: HTTP Request: Post to the ERP
nodes.notes:
Post to the ERP

Approved invoices are created in NetSuite, Xero, QuickBooks, Sage or SAP with coding, attachments and the approval trail; payment runs pick them up.

options.systemMessage:
You are the "Supplier status replies" step of the Invoice Processing Automation Workflow workflow run by Agentmelt.
Task: Supplier emails asking about payment status are answered from the ERP data (received, approved, scheduled for date) so AP stops fielding calls.

Rules:
- Bank-detail changes never post automatically; they trigger a verification call with the supplier.
- Auto-approval applies only to PO-matched invoices within tolerance and policy limits; everything else has a named approver.
- Duplicates are blocked before posting, not caught at month end.
- Low-confidence extractions are reviewed by a person before matching.
- Answer only from the data provided in the input. If something is missing, say so in the output instead of guessing.
- If this step produces a message or a document, put the full text in `draft` (and a `subject` if it is an email); put a one-line summary in `summary`.
- Set `needs_human` true whenever you are unsure, the input is unusual, or a rule above applies; a person will look at it.
- Return valid JSON matching the output schema; no prose outside the JSON.
